question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: a JSON-RPC tools/call of hf_whoami with empty arguments, on a session opened by an initialize in the same second (clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0); content-type application/json, accept application/json, text/event-stream; no Authorization header, no cookie

decoded.what-it-answered: a tools/call result with isError absent, one text block headed "# Hugging Face authentication" reading "The Hugging Face tools are being used anonymously and may be rate limited." and pointing to https://hf.co/settings/mcp/ and https://hf.co/join, and a structuredContent object: status "anonymous", account null, organizations [], credential null, guidance (the same two links). The body is appendix A7 of the artifact, whole.
decoded.why-this-record-exists: it is the server's own statement of what the keyless caller is. A tool whose documented purpose is to "inspect the current Hugging Face authentication context" answered an anonymous caller with a structured status of anonymous rather than an error, a 401 or a demand for a token. The entry's noAccountNeeded cell rests on this and on the docs search record, not on the handshake alone.
decoded.the-same-answer-twice: a hand-sent hf_whoami at 06:05:33Z on another session answered with the same text and the same structuredContent (the first-pass transcript is in the researcher's run log, not the artifact; the 06:07:17Z request is the one recorded here). Two readings two minutes apart are consistency, not a rate.
decoded.the-status-line-read: the origin's status is the SECOND HTTP line in the artifact; this container's egress proxy answers CONNECT with its own HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established first.
decoded.not-measured: what the tool returns to a token holder (nothing was sent); whether "may be rate limited" has a number on the MCP path (no RateLimit header on any MCP response; the vendor's rate-limit page tabulates 500 Hub API requests per 5 minutes per anonymous IP, and does not say which bucket MCP calls draw from).
decoded.where-the-artifact-is: the transcript is the appendix dated 2026-10-03 at the end of the registry-sweep artifact linked below (sections 1, 1b, 2, 3, 4 and A1 to A9), placed there because the researcher's site is at its publisher's 200-file cap; the appendix is verbatim and the session ids are redacted.

finding: A keyless tools/call of hf_whoami on https://huggingface.co/mcp answered HTTP 200 on 2026-10-03 at 06:07:17Z with structuredContent status "anonymous", account null, credential null, and a text block saying "The Hugging Face tools are being used anonymously and may be rate limited" with the vendor's two links for a token or an account. The surface states its own keyless condition in a machine-readable field, which is the strongest form of the disclosure the registry asks of a keyless path: not an inference from a 200, but the server's own word for what the caller is. Which rate limit applies to MCP calls is not stated by the server or by the vendor's rate-limit page, whose anonymous Hub API row is 500 requests per 5 minutes per IP; no RateLimit header was served on this path.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -X POST https://huggingface.co/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'Mcp-Session-Id: <the id an initialize response carried>' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"hf_whoami","arguments":{}}}'
